Selah.' and web:Ps.32.8 opens a new first-person voice, 'I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go' -- a genuine speech/discourse-frame shift (tier-1) from the confessing psalmist to an instructing voice addressing him, independent of the corroborating selah at v7 (pmarks_Ps.json: Ps.32.7=1, consistent with the row's own disclosure). 'medium' confidence reads conservative given the strength of the speech-frame driver, but under-confidence is not a material defect and I do not challenge it.

web_mt_offset_map.json confirms Ps 33 is identity with web_title=false and no superscription entry in psalm_device_inventory.json -- the row's 'carries no WEB title' claim is correct, and the acrostics table (9,10,25,34,37,111,112,119,145) omits 33, confirming the device_notes' disclaimer that no acrostic scheme is claimed despite the 22-verse/22-letter coincidence. All 3 imperative quotes (oshb:Ps.33.1, 33.2, 33.3) collate at byte tier (3/3) and are true 2mp imperative forms, distinct in kind from the later 3rd-person prefix-conjugation clause at MT 33:8 -- so the row's underlying 'congregational imperative' boundary at v3 is grammatically defensible. Two independent, tool-confirmed evidence-discipline defects remain (below); neither overturns the span, but both are material per the binding register rules this campaign enforces symmetrically on rows and challenges alike.

MT Ps.33.8 opens יִֽירְא֣וּ מֵ֭יְהוָה כָּל ('Let all the earth fear...', WEB) -- a 3rd-person yiqtol/jussive form, grammatically distinct from the 2mp imperatives of 33:1-3, so the row's implicit congregational-vs-universal distinction likely survives scrutiny -- but as written the claim supplies no swept count naming its unit and does not disclose or rule out this nearest candidate, which the campaign's own count-object discipline requires.

reviews.reasoning: verse_map_web.json confirms the topical arc: v4 opens a motive clause ('For Yahweh's word is right'), v6 develops creation-by-word ('By Yahweh's word, the heavens were made'), v9 closes the creation sub-unit on a fitting echo ('he spoke, and it was done'), and v10-11 pivots to the nations/Yahweh's-counsel antithesis, closing on 'The counsel of Yahweh stands fast forever.' All three cited Hebrew quotes (oshb:Ps.33.4, 33.6, 33.11) collate at byte tier. pmarks_Ps.json confirms no selah anywhere in Ps 33 and the sole paseq in this psalm (Ps.33.12) falls outside this span, so device_notes' narrower claim ('no selah or acrostic marker') is accurate and -- unlike M8-Ps-081 -- does not overclaim into the full marks-layer. The rejected_alternative's claim that v4-9 and v10-11 share 'no addressee, speaker, or imperative-mood signal' marking a seam is consistent with the verse text; the unit is topically coherent across all 8 verses of the span (33:4-11) as one sustained meditation on Yahweh's word, and I find no stronger rival tier-1 seam one verse away. 'medium' confidence is appropriate for a topically- rather than marks-driven unit.

verse_map_web.json confirms the reopening beatitude at v12 ('Blessed is the nation whose God is Yahweh'), widening through Yahweh's oversight of humankind (v13-15), the futility of military strength (v16-17), and closing on the eye-of-Yahweh providence motif spanning v18-19 (deliverance 'from death'/'in famine'). Both cited quotes (oshb:Ps.33.12, 33.18) collate at byte tier (2/2). The cross-psalm ashrei-particle parallel to web:Ps.32.1-2 is correctly flagged as texture rather than a boundary relation (device_notes explicitly disclaims a cross-psalm merge), consistent with the book strategy's rule that recurring formulas are texture, never drivers by themselves -- and since Ps 32 and Ps 33 are different parent psalms this is not a same-psalm seam-cohesion concern requiring resolution either way. No selah or paseq falls in this span (pmarks_Ps.json). I find the three-beat internal movement (elect nation -> universal oversight -> military futility -> providence close) coherent as a single strophe rather than a rival split at v15/16; 'medium' confidence matches a formulaic-recognition warrant rather than a hard tier-1 marker.

verse_map_web.json confirms a clean person/voice shift at v20 ('Our soul has waited for Yahweh. He is our help and our shield') from the third-person 'him/his' providence language of v13-19 to a plural congregational 'our/we' voice sustained through the closing petition at v22 ('Let your loving kindness be on us, Yahweh'). Both cited quotes (oshb:Ps.33.20, 33.22) collate at byte tier (2/2). pmarks_Ps.json confirms no selah, and the psalm carries no book-boundary doxology (Ps 33 is not among 41/72/89/106) and no acrostic entry, so device_notes' 'no selah, doxology, or acrostic marker' claim is accurate and appropriately scoped (it does not repeat the M8-Ps-081-style marks-layer overclaim). This is the strongest-warranted seam in the psalm's second half -- a genuine tier-1 discourse-frame shift -- and 'high' confidence is justified.
